chunks: And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave who accuses the free man, how many lashes is he given? He said: Forty.
Thus we have explained the reasoning in this narration in the report of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, so there is no need to repeat it, and it adds to what we mentioned as clarification.
ai.seo_question: How many lashes does Islamic jurisprudence determine the punishment for a slave who accuses a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the specific penalty of forty lashes for a slave (mamluk) accused of qadhf (false accusation of zina) against a free man, reflecting the jurisprudential principle that slaves receive half the punishment of free individuals. Shaykh al-Tusi notes that the legal reasoning (wajh) was already detailed in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, demonstrating the compiler's method of avoiding redundancy while maintaining comprehensive legal coverage. This ruling highlights the social stratification in classical Shia fiqh, where status influences the severity of hudud penalties.
